title: Exact Evaluation of Trigonometric Functions on the Unit Circle
originalTopic: Unit Circle Evaluation and Reference Angles
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the reference angle and determine the exact values of sin(5*pi/6), cos(5*pi/6), and tan(5*pi/6).

steps.title: Identify Quadrant and Reference Angle
steps.explanation: Since pi/2 < 5*pi/6 < pi, the terminal ray lies in the second quadrant. The reference angle formed with the negative x-axis is pi - 5*pi/6 = pi/6 (or 30 degrees).
steps.why: Reference angles to the horizontal axis determine trigonometric magnitudes.

steps.title: Determine Algebraic Signs in Quadrant II
steps.explanation: In Quadrant II, the x-coordinate is negative and the y-coordinate is positive. Therefore, sine is positive, while cosine and tangent are negative.
steps.why: Cartesian signs of coordinate points on the unit circle define trigonometric signs.

steps.title: Calculate Exact Values
steps.explanation: Apply the standard special triangle values for pi/6 combined with the respective quadrant signs.
steps.why: Evaluation via reference angles and quadrant sign rules produces exact values.
